# Contributing to fireSense

Each module chapter in this manual is generated from that module's own
`.Rmd` file, in the module's repository -- not from anything stored here.
To correct or extend a chapter, edit `<module>/<module>.Rmd` in the module
repository and the change reaches this manual on its next build.

This manual rebuilds daily, and on every push to its `main` branch. It checks
each module out by branch rather than pinning a commit, so a merged
documentation change appears here without anyone updating this repository.
The branch each module is tracked at is listed in
`.github/workflows/firesense-manual.yaml`.

## What lives where

Some of what appears in a chapter is not prose at all. The tables of inputs,
parameters and outputs are generated from the module's metadata, so they are
corrected by editing the module's `defineModule()` call rather than its `.Rmd`.
References belong in the module's `citations/references_<module>.bib`.

## Headings

A module `.Rmd` is knitted on its own as well as being a chapter here, but in the
book its headings share one namespace with every other chapter. Give the file a
single level-1 heading -- `# <module> Module` -- and make everything below it
level 2 or deeper. A module that uses level-1 headings for its own sections
contributes one top-level chapter per heading to the book, and generic ones such
as `# Overview` or `# Parameters` then appear as chapters in their own right.

## Adding a module

Three things need to change together: a checkout step in the workflow, a chapter
entry in `_bookdown.yml`, and the module list in the Overview. A module fetched
but not listed as a chapter is silently absent from the book.
